competencies.text: Discuss properties of sound waves in communications, navigation, medicine, and entertainment.
Identify innovations such as soundproofing, amplifiers, and sonar.

days.title: Nature of Sound Waves
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to describe how sound travels as a mechanical wave, explain frequency, wavelength, amplitude, and speed of sound, and identify how sound is used in communication, navigation, medicine, and entertainment.

🔊 What Is Sound?

Sound is a mechanical wave — a vibration that travels through a medium (solid, liquid, or gas). Unlike light, sound cannot travel through a vacuum because it needs particles to vibrate.

Sound travels fastest through solids, slower through liquids, and slowest through gases.

MediumSpeed of Sound
Air (20°C)~343 m/s
Water~1,480 m/s
Steel~5,960 m/s

📊 Key Properties of Sound

PropertyWhat It MeansWhat You Hear
FrequencyNumber of vibrations per second (Hz)Pitch — high or low
WavelengthDistance between two consecutive compressionsRelated to pitch
AmplitudeHeight of the waveVolume — loud or soft
SpeedHow fast sound travels through a mediumDetermines echo delay

🎼 Pitch, Frequency & the Human Ear

Humans can hear frequencies between 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz (20 kHz).

  • Infrasonic (below 20 Hz) — elephants and earthquakes produce these.
  • Ultrasonic (above 20 kHz) — bats, dolphins, and medical imaging use these.

As we age, we lose the ability to hear high frequencies.

🎵 Sound Wave Types

  • Longitudinal waves: Particles vibrate parallel to the direction of the wave. This is how sound travels through air.
  • Compression: Where particles are packed together (high pressure).
  • Rarefaction: Where particles are spread apart (low pressure).

🔊 Real-Life Applications

  • Communications: Telephones, radio, microphones and speakers.
  • Navigation: Sonar (SOund Navigation And Ranging) — used by submarines and fishing boats.
  • Medicine: Ultrasound imaging for pregnancy, echocardiograms, and kidney stones treatment.
  • Entertainment: Musical instruments, concerts, surround-sound speakers, cinema audio.

🛠️ Modern Sound Innovations

  • Soundproofing: Materials like foam, acoustic tiles, and double-glazed windows absorb sound to prevent noise pollution.
  • Amplifiers: Increase the amplitude of sound waves for concerts and PA systems.
  • Noise-cancelling headphones: Emit inverse sound waves to cancel out background noise.
  • Ultrasound devices: Used for cleaning jewelry, medical imaging, and even repelling mosquitoes.

💡 Fun Fact

The loudest sound ever recorded was the Krakatoa volcano eruption in 1883 — heard 4,800 km away in Australia. That's because low-frequency sound waves travel incredibly far.

📌 Quick Check

  • Why can't sound travel through space? (Answer: no particles to vibrate)
  • What happens to pitch when frequency increases? (Answer: pitch goes higher)
  • What does SONAR stand for? (Answer: SOund Navigation And Ranging)

days.title: Match Game — Sound Technologies
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each sound concept or technology to its correct description or example. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Number of vibrations per second (Hz) — determines pitch
Height of the sound wave — determines volume
Particles vibrate parallel to direction of travel — how sound moves through air
Uses reflected sound waves to detect underwater objects
Sound above 20,000 Hz — used for medical imaging
Foam, acoustic tiles, double-glazed windows that absorb sound
Increases the amplitude of sound waves for concerts and PA systems
Reflected sound wave you hear after the original sound

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Sound Around Us
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🚢 A fishing boat uses sonar to locate schools of fish. What property of sound makes this possible?

choices.label: A) Sound waves travel faster in air
B) Sound waves reflect off objects, and the echo timing reveals distance
D) Sound waves have zero frequency underwater

scenario.text: 🎤 A singer on stage uses a microphone connected to a speaker. What is the speaker's main function?

choices.label: B) To amplify sound by increasing amplitude

scenario.text: 🤰 A pregnant mother undergoes an ultrasound. What makes ultrasound safer than X-rays for imaging a fetus?

choices.label: A) Ultrasound uses high-energy waves that pass through the body
B) Ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves (not ionizing radiation), making it safe for the developing baby
C) Ultrasound is a type of light wave
D) Ultrasound works by heating the tissues

scenario.text: 🎧 You are in a noisy jeepney and wearing noise-cancelling headphones. How do they reduce the noise?

choices.label: A) By blocking all sound waves with foam
B) By emitting inverse sound waves that cancel out background noise
D) By reducing the speed of sound

scenario.text: 🎼 A guitarist plucks a string harder and hears a louder sound. Which property of the sound wave increased?
